notes.note:
The mods button opens Vortex at the server's revision
- The button on the mods card now opens Vortex straight at the collection revision the server runs, with no web page in between.
- When Vortex is done, the launcher scans and fixes by itself, so nobody has to press Scan and Fix.

Downloads page names the publisher
- The line under the installer's button now names who signed it, the same name Windows shows when you run it.

The character choice answers the mouse again
- A click on the character choice while the game is still loading no longer picks whoever stands in the middle of the screen.
- Once the cursor shows, the choice follows the mouse and a click joins as that character.

The launcher's version is now a date
- The number under the launcher's name is the day and time it last changed, so a newer launcher always has a higher one

bodies.body:
<!-- Thank you for sending a change. Fill in the first three parts. The part under
"For the Thornswood team" is the team's own checklist: if you are not on the team,
leave it as it is. CONTRIBUTING.md says how a change gets here. -->

## What changed

<!-- What a person will notice, in plain words, and why. If it fixes a problem, say
what caused it and how you found that out: a log line, a file, the steps. One
change per pull request. -->

## How you checked it

<!-- What you ran or did, and what you saw. "Not checked" is an answer too; leave
nothing blank. -->

## Release note

<!-- What people read about this change in the launcher's News, on the site and
in Discord. A headline of three words or more, then at least one line starting
with "- " directly under it. Plain words: never the banned word, no em dashes, no issue
or pull request numbers, no file or code names, no version in the headline.
"Release note: none" when nobody would notice the change in the game, the
launcher, the site or Discord. The "Release note" check reads it, and the
release carries it as written. -->

Release note: 

## Before you send it

- [ ] It changes one thing.
- [ ] It removes the cause of the problem, not only what shows of it.
- [ ] I have read LICENSE and LICENSING.md, which say what a contribution is given under.

Whose work: mine
<!-- "Mine" when everything in it is yours. Otherwise name each part that is somebody else's, who it belongs to and how they gave leave (LICENSING.md, contributor term 3). -->

## For the Thornswood team

<!-- Closes #N when it finishes an issue nobody would notice. A fix people would notice
says Refs #N and carries its test task, which moves the issue to Done on merge.
That issue stays open until a main Ship puts the fix on the main server, and that
Ship closes it with this test task; never close it at the merge, or testers are
sent to look for a fix main lacks. Main if any playtester can check it with the
normal game (even if a dev command would be quicker); plain words, no numbers,
links, code or "dev":
Test task for #N: <title, at most 45 characters>
Server: Main
1. Plain steps.
What should happen: what the tester sees.
Dev only if it needs staff or dev commands, the dev server, logs, the box or a
setup testers cannot make; developer terms, posted for staff as soon as a build
carries it, and it stays while the fix is on main:
Test task for #N: <title, at most 45 characters>
Server: Dev
Build: <the dev release or commit it needs>
1. Steps with the files, commands and log lines.
What should happen: what each prints or shows.
One test task per issue and kind; never post one by hand in Discord. The
check "Test tasks in the pull request" holds every block to the bot's post
rules before the merge; when it is red, edit this body and it runs again.
Test task comments and known-issue text carry no footer: no closing "---" line
and no "Generated by" line.
Developer-Guide.md, "Test tasks and known issues". -->

### Which parts it touches, and what runs after the merge

<!-- Tick every part this pull request changes. Each line is one row of the table
in Developer-Guide.md, "After a pull request is merged", and the command for it is
in that table, the one copy of them. They all run in the same sitting. -->

- [ ] The launcher (`launcher\app`, `launcher\ui.xaml`), the game plugins (`game\plugins`) or anything else in a pack
- [ ] The gamemode on the dev server
- [ ] The gamemode on the live server (`game\gamemode.js`) or the content plugin (`game\content\Thornswood-Content.esp`), whose server command goes before the Ship
- [ ] The live server build, or the live settings
- [ ] The site's app or `site\public`
- [ ] The public pages (`site\data\site\*.md`)
- [ ] The bot's code or join card art (`bot`)
- [ ] The bot's avatar (`bot\thornswood-bot-*.png`), which no script sends
- [ ] The voice service (`voice\voice-server.js`, `voice\headlines.js`)
- [ ] Only scripts that change how a release is built
- [ ] Docs only

### Before asking for a read

- [ ] It says what the cause was. No band-aids: nothing that notices the damage and undoes it, no retry that hopes a race comes out right, no layer over an earlier band-aid (Developer-Guide.md, "Fix the cause, no band-aids").
- [ ] If it edits Shell.cs, Checks.cs, Keep.cs, Hold.cs, Updater.cs or Publish-Update.ps1 in a way that blocks others' work, a line went in #dev-coordination about it first, as Developer-Guide.md, "Signing, the build check, and the six shared files", says. No line anywhere for opening or merging the pull request itself.
- [ ] If it changes anything in Developer-Guide.md's settled design, the team agreed it in #staff-updates first.
- [ ] Anything it found or left unfinished is on the board (GitHub Issues).
